display.title: The Baal Shem Tov to the Rescue: The Kidnapped Boy
display.summary_short: Years after the Baal Shem Tov's passing, a boy born through his blessing is kidnapped by a poritz, and following the tzaddik's instructions, his father finds him with the help of a mysterious 'bishop'.
display.summary_long: A childless student of the Baal Shem Tov is blessed with a son, on condition that the boy is guarded like the apple of his eye. Three years after the Baal Shem Tov passes away, the babysitter steps out to watch a dancing bear, and five-year-old Moshele vanishes. The father turns to Adel, the Baal Shem Tov's daughter, who goes to her father's resting place and returns with instructions: stop at every inn and tell the innkeeper. For months he finds nothing, but he refuses to skip a single inn, and at last an innkeeper tells him that an old poritz has taken a Jewish boy to raise as his heir and is waiting for a bishop to convert him. The father stops the bishop's carriage on the road. The 'bishop' tells the poritz that a Jewish child will always run to a fellow Jew, and when they step outside, Moshele runs straight into his father's arms. On the way home the father passes the real bishop, who arrives late. Adel tells him that his carelessness gave her father a lot of trouble. The storyteller ends with the lesson of following the Rebbe's instructions as we draw closer to Moshiach.
display.lesson: Follow a tzaddik's instructions fully, without skipping any part, and never give up. A Jewish child always stays connected to his people.

advisories.note: A five-year-old is kidnapped and held for months; resolved happily.
A poritz plans to have the boy converted and raised as a non-Jew.
